- **KB-2 (note, task 0)**: partial mirror above.
- **KB-3 (realism)**: impossible worked inputs — `pending_month_cost_of_care_calculation_0565b7b1` "24 days booked in benefit days 1 through 20" in one 30-day month, and `estimate_reconciliation_calculation_e8c8c0ae` "Part A days covered in full | 26" in a 31-day month; at most 20 days of a benefit period fall in days 1–20, and a second benefit period cannot begin within the same month.
- **KB-4 (rounding wording)**: `hospice_room_board_and_collection_terms_d3f51913` illustration "251.80 multiplied by 95, divided by 100, rounded half up to the cent" rounds the per-day share, a step the source never takes (compute rounds the share-day kind total); a per-day reading gives 1910.93 / 334.97 / 231.63 on task 0. The governing share document is correct and the illustration is disclaimed, so the blind audit was not misled.

## Source-side problems (do not change this verdict)
- **SRC-1**: the assembly sentences of the rule (`funds_part` "figures entering the funds … a figure entering the advance itself is added after that"; pending "figures entering the estimate … figures entering the advance …"; day pricing "every day that neither the standard pricing nor a schedule takes out …") presuppose figures beyond the baseline, so their only faithful home — the computation document — signals that variations exist ("not taken out", "a figure entering the advance itself").
- **SRC-2**: approved baseline.rule carries "An allowance the case does not record counts as zero", a quantity only approved_amount_kept uses (XF A.3).
- **SRC-3**: pending refund overwrite caps the applied credit at "the figure that month will carry", while pending_balance_carried_in caps it at "the base estimate figure" (no effect in either task).
- **SRC-4**: parameter meanings `cost_of_care_cap` ("at the Medicaid daily rate"), `partial_month_basis` and `refund_days` restate base clauses that the overwrites qualify; their parameter documents (`cost_of_care_and_payment_in_full_4aae7a36` "never set above what the month's care costs at the Medicaid daily rate", partial-month bullet; `payment_refund_and_closing_terms_f633afb4` "A credit balance is refunded within 30 calendar days of arising") state them unqualified beside the retired-surface documents.
- **SRC-5**: approved_amount_kept's tier condition rests on Resident Trust Fund Accounts tier setting `medicaid_pna_retained` (trust not yet published) — figure 45.00 conditional.
- Cross-product owed writes: medicare (correct_coinsurance_rate, pay_coinsurance_by_card/bank_draft, post_coinsurance_charge, reduce_coinsurance_for_reversed_days) and bedhold (opening/closing/stay charges) tools write charges, payments, rate corrections or adjustments that no scored read uses (coinsurance price reads liable parties; held-day factors read bookings, not charges) — none moves a scored read. Trust writes: conditional (unpublished).
- PA MA figures stated (PNA 45.00, VA 90.00 under 38 U.S.C. 5503(d), HMA 6 months, retro 3, look-back 60, hearing 30 / continuation 10 days, renewal 12, 45/90-day standards, hospice 95%, COLA January, Part B 202.90, SNF coinsurance 217.00 / 209.50) are realistic.

**SEED-1 (gold-moving).** Both worlds keep one continuous Part A episode across a hospital absence of three midnights — task 0: departure 2026-09-26 18:40, return 09-29 (bed-hold 1431d92d); task 1: departure 10-26 19:05, return 10-29 (0342fd8c). `qualifying_stay_and_transfer_windows_7fdf5798`: "Interrupted-stay window: consecutive calendar days within which a return to the same center continues the same coverage episode | 3 days (return by 12:00 a.m. of the third day)"; `one_open_episode_rule_e2edacbc`: "a return after that window opens a new episode once the earlier one has ended"; `nomnc_and_coverage_end_96dd9af5`: coverage ends without NOMNC "when a hospital transfer is not followed by a return within the interrupted-stay window (hospital transfer, no return)". Counting the departure day as day 1 (the PDPM interrupted-stay convention the charter cites) the window is 26–28 (task 0) / 26–28 (task 1); counting from the day after departure, a return on the third day comes after "12:00 a.m. of the third day". Under either reading the return on the 29th is outside the window, so the published Medicare documents produce an ended episode (hospital transfer, no return) and a new episode from the 29th. Effect on Medicaid reads: task 0 — the actual-month review covers only a resident with "exactly one coverage episode under Medicare Part A" (two → no Oct reduction), and September fails "the month's Part A days were all booked by the resident's coverage with the latest coverage start" (→ not priced day by day; cost 24 × 287.36 = 6,896.64; no reconciliation reduction); task 1 — October fails the same test (→ cost 22 × 279.84 = 6,156.48; no reduction). Every scored value of both tasks moves. (The docs' window figure carries no day-1 anchor; that wording gap is part of this item.)
